subject.title: fix(sessions): add try-catch wrappers around unprotected JSON.parse calls in session-accessor.sqlite.ts

question: When canonical transcript_events.event_json is malformed, should runtime fail the affected operation and require doctor repair, or expose an explicit degraded or quarantine result that preserves row identity?
rationale: The PR chooses silent row loss and fail-open identity behavior, but database-first policy requires an intentional owner and contract for persistent corruption; code review cannot safely choose the user-visible recovery semantics.

options.title: Fail closed plus doctor repair
options.body: Return a structured corruption failure from runtime reads and add or reuse a doctor repair or quarantine path so canonical events are never silently discarded.

options.title: Explicit degraded read
options.body: Return a surfaced degraded result that preserves event-to-row alignment and blocks identity reuse while allowing carefully bounded read-only access to valid rows.

options.title: Keep current throwing behavior
options.body: Leave the unguarded parse behavior until a complete corruption diagnosis and repair design is ready rather than merging silent partial-state semantics.

recommendation.title: Fail closed plus doctor repair
recommendation.body: Return a structured corruption failure from runtime reads and add or reuse a doctor repair or quarantine path so canonical events are never silently discarded.

likelyOwner.reason: Their database-first SQLite work is the strongest available provenance for canonical state, migration, and repair ownership.
